record_identity.title: Biometric non-verification converted into essential public-benefit suspension

summary: A biometric or algorithmic identity-verification failure is treated as sufficient basis to suspend, interrupt, or materially burden access to an essential public benefit even though non-verification is not proof of ineligibility, fraud, identity mismatch, or lawful revocation.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Essential public benefits can be necessary for food, housing, health and basic subsistence. A failed biometric check must remain a verification-state problem rather than silently becoming an adverse entitlement decision.

source_records.source_title: Incident 1606: SASSA Facial-Verification Failures Reportedly Contributed to Social Grant Access Disruptions in South Africa
source_records.system_or_product: SASSA eLife Certification portal and social-grant review workflow
source_records.deployment_context: South African social-grant verification and suspension workflow
source_records.source_context: AIID reports facial-recognition failure among non-verification causes and 67,868 grant suspensions for the quarter, while not establishing how many suspensions were caused specifically by facial verification.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports the distinction between biometric non-verification and lawful entitlement suspension while preserving the aggregate-count limitation.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct public web review in this intake
limitations: The 67,868 suspension total must not be attributed solely to facial-verification failure.

contextual_relations.rationale: PROP-0023 separates inability to verify from entitlement invalidity in a different domain; public-benefit governance requires a fresh coverage assessment rather than automatic reuse.

failure_mode_definition: A failure occurs when inability to complete biometric verification is operationally promoted into benefit suspension, denial or material burden without independent eligibility determination, proportionate fallback, notice and contestability.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met when biometric non-verification changes an essential-benefit state or blocks practical access without independent evidence of ineligibility, fraud or lawful revocation and without a proportionate alternative verification pathway.

failure_classification.failure_scope: essential public-benefit systems using biometric or algorithmic identity verification
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: recurs where non-verification is allowed to change entitlement state without independent adjudication
failure_classification.persistence: may persist until verification or benefit status is independently corrected
failure_classification.reproducibility: can be tested with failed-verification scenarios and valid-entitlement controls
failure_classification.visibility: may appear procedurally valid if verification state and entitlement state are collapsed
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects a credible pathway to loss of essential subsistence support and procedural exclusion; it does not imply that every suspension in the cited aggregate was biometric-caused.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_gap: The reviewed evidence does not establish how many of the 67,868 suspensions were caused specifically by facial-verification failure.
